description: Verify two scientific claims against real abstracts: one is supported, one is contradicted, and one paper is unrelated. Cite the evidence for each verdict.
task_prompt:
Two claims are under review.
Claim 1: Noninvasive positive pressure ventilation is not predictive of acute respiratory failure after solid organ transplantation.
Claim 2: Phase information is useful for predicting donor-recipient matches in organ transplantation.
Using the papers in documents/, decide for each claim whether the evidence supports or contradicts it. Write each verdict on its own line as 'Claim N: SUPPORTED' or 'Claim N: CONTRADICTED'. For each verdict, cite the paper and the specific result behind it.

seeds.text: Phase information is useful for predicting donor-recipient matches in organ transplantation.
rationale: Genes that influence transplantation outcome could be identified by using linkage disequilibrium (LD)-mapping approaches, if the extended MHC haplotypes of the unrelated donor and recipient could be defined.

seeds.text: Noninvasive positive pressure ventilation is not predictive of acute respiratory failure after solid organ transplantation.
rationale: Within the first hour of treatment, 14 patients (70%) in the NIV group, and 5 patients (25%) in the standard treatment group improved their ratio of the PaO2 to the fraction of inspired oxygen (FIO2).
Over time, a sustained improvement in PaO2 to FIO2 was noted in 12 patients (60%) in the NIV group, and in 5 patients (25%) randomized to standard treatment (P = .03).

The use of NIV was associated with a significant reduction in the rate of endotracheal intubation (20% vs 70%; P = .002), rate of fatal complications (20% vs 50%; P = .05), length of stay in the intensive care unit by survivors (mean [SD] days, 5.5 [3] vs 9 [4]; P = .03), and intensive care unit mortality (20% vs 50%; P = .05).
CONCLUSIONS These results indicate that transplantation programs should consider NIV in the treatment of selected recipients of transplantation with acute respiratory failure.

claim_2_verdict.description: Claim 2 is supported by the evidence
claim_2_verdict.claim: Phase information is useful for predicting donor-recipient matches in organ transplantation.

claim_1_verdict.description: Claim 1 is contradicted by the evidence
claim_1_verdict.claim: Noninvasive positive pressure ventilation is not predictive of acute respiratory failure after solid organ transplantation.
